title: All Quiet on the Western Front

evidence.note: Published by Universal Pictures in 1930 (US premiere April 21, 1930). The 95-year US copyright term expired December 31, 2025, so the photoplay entered the US public domain on January 1, 2026. Term expiry is a bright line, independent of the film's separate (and likely absent) 28-year renewal.
evidence.source: US Copyright Office — Duration of Copyright

evidence.note: Confirmed as a 1930-class work entering the US public domain on Public Domain Day, January 1, 2026.
evidence.source: Duke Center for the Study of the Public Domain — Public Domain Day 2026

evidence.note: The film's recorded music (musical direction David Broekman) was published integral to the 1930 sound release rather than as a separately registered and renewed song score, so it shares the film's 1930 term and is US public domain as of 2026. This differs from cases like Charade, where a separately renewed song score survived the film's own expiry.

Adapted from Erich Maria Remarque's novel 'Im Westen nichts Neues' (English 'All Quiet on the Western Front', trans. A.W. Wheen), first published 1929. A 1929 work's maximum US term (95 years from publication) expired end of 2024, so the underlying story entered the US public domain on January 1, 2025 — before the film itself.

The novel is a German (foreign) work, so URAA (17 U.S.C. §104A; Golan v. Holder) could have restored its US copyright — but URAA restoration runs only for the same 95-years-from-publication term, which for a 1929 work has already expired. Restoration therefore does not revive it.

No active franchise-character or title trademark known to bar reuse of the 1930 film. The title was later reused for a 1979 CBS TV movie and a 2022 German-language Netflix production, but those are separate works, not a mark blocking the 1930 photoplay. Confirm current marks before branded commercial use.

Modern restored transfers exist (Universal restoration and archival preservation elements) and circulate as 4K 'Blu-ray remux' copies. A remaster carries a thin derivative copyright in the new transfer, not in the 1930 film. Reuse an archival print rather than a studio disc rip.

editorial:
All Quiet on the Western Front is Universal's 1930 adaptation of Erich Maria Remarque's anti-war novel, directed by Lewis Milestone and produced by 21-year-old Carl Laemmle Jr. It swept the third Academy Awards, winning Outstanding Production and Best Director, and its trench work — the tracking shots along the parapet, the final reach for a butterfly — still defines how the First World War looks on screen. Universal issued it in both sound and silent versions in 1930, and on January 1, 2026 its 95-year US copyright term expired, so the photoplay is now public domain in the United States by term, with no renewal analysis required.

The clean part is unusually clean here. The recorded 1930 soundtrack was published as part of the film and shares its expired term, and even the underlying German novel — first published in 1929 — has already run out its own 95-year US term, so the story layer is free too. The one trap that actually applies is the restoration: Universal and archival institutions have produced modern restored transfers, and the 4K 'Blu-ray remux' copies now circulating carry a thin derivative copyright in the remaster, not in the film. For reuse, pull an archival print (the long-standing Internet Archive copies below) rather than a studio disc rip, and you are on the safest possible footing.
faq: Is All Quiet on the Western Front (1930) public domain in the US?

Yes. Its 95-year copyright term expired and the film entered the US public domain on January 1, 2026, so the photoplay is free to use regardless of the old renewal question. The 1929 source novel is likewise past its US term.
Can I sell or monetize copies of the film?

The 1930 print, its soundtrack, and the underlying story are all public domain in the US, so yes — but don't rip a modern Universal restoration or 4K remaster, whose remastered picture and audio carry a separate derivative copyright. Use an archival transfer.
